author: Karl Rock
description:
One of the most interesting things I noticed while travelling around Karachi was just how late the city stays awake. Karachiites seem to be serious night owls.

Shops stay open late, restaurants can be serving customers well past midnight, and it’s not unusual for the city to still feel alive at 2 or even 3 AM.

It felt noticeably different from many other parts of Pakistan, where things tend to wind down earlier. Karachi’s late-night culture is a big part of the city’s character.

So if you want to get stuff done without the crowds, do it in the morning... as long as where you want to go is open.
title: Karachi is NOT for early birds!

author: Karl Rock
description:
In Pakistan, you can find tradies and day labourers waiting along busy roads for work. Each morning, workers gather in designated spots, often carrying the tools they need, and wait for contractors or other people looking for workers to stop and hire them for the day.

It’s a simple system that connects people looking for work with those who need extra labour, with workers typically paid a daily wage depending on the type of work and their skills.

I came across these roadside labour markets while travelling through Pakistan and found it fascinating to see how people find work in a very informal economy.
title: How To Hire Tradies... in Pakistan
